title: Pseudocode
body:
The [[Algorithm]] written in something between English and code: precise about the steps, silent
about the syntax. It exists so that the planning stage and the typing stage are separate
problems.

```
GET price
GET tax_rate
SET total TO price * (1 + tax_rate)
IF total > 100 THEN
    SET total TO total * 0.9
DISPLAY total
```

That is not [[Python]], and it is not meant to be. It commits to the *logic* (there is a
discount, it applies after tax, the threshold is 100) and refuses to commit to anything a
language would force you to decide.

**Why bother when you could just write the code.** Because the two kinds of mistake are found
differently. A logic mistake in pseudocode costs one line of rewriting; the same mistake found
after the program is written costs a debugging session. This is Polya's second step in
[[Algorithm]], "plan solution", made concrete, and it is the step everyone skips.

There is no standard. Anything unambiguous is correct pseudocode, and the conventions worth
keeping are the ones that stop it drifting back into a language: capitalised keywords, indented
blocks, `SET`/`GET`/`DISPLAY` rather than `=`/`input`/`print`.

Related planning tools in [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]], each answering a different
question: [[IPO Diagram]] for what goes in and comes out, [[Structure chart]] for how the
functions divide the work, [[Program design]] for the whole procedure. Pseudocode is the one that
carries the **order of operations**, which is why the [[Tracing Table]] is built from it.
